data.claim: Lease renewals (43% of events, 15% of bytes) and gate evidence (gate.passed+failed: 35% of events? no: 17% of events, 50% of bytes) dominate; the fold cost is dominated by dataclasses.asdict in records._claim, so a flat copy cuts status time by >=20% with a byte-identical fold.
data.falsifier: status time not reduced by the flat claim copy, or fold(repr items) differs from the asdict version on this repository's real log.
data.mechanism: _claim runs asdict (deep copy) three times per lease.renewed during fold; renewals are 27.5k of 63.5k events. Coalescing renewals and moving evidence bodies out of the shards shrink parse and fold input.

After asdict fix: status 5.35s next 2.92s on the real log; tests/test_log_scale.py compares repr(fold(...).items) with the asdict claim on the real log: identical. Renewal-gap simulation on the real log: W=120s keeps 19.1k of 27.5k renewals, W=300s 8.8k, W=600s 5.9k, W=900s 4.4k.

data.claim: Loading a pickled folded State is faster than folding the same events.
data.falsifier: pickle.loads(State) takes about as long as fold(events), or longer.
data.mechanism: A checkpoint replaces an O(N) fold with an O(N) load plus an O(tail) fold; it pays only when the load is cheaper than the fold.
data.probe: python3: st=fold(events,strict=False) 0.213 s; pickle.dumps(st,protocol=5) 0.225 s -> 31.96 MB; pickle.loads 0.213 s; repr(items) identical
data.probe_output: fold 0.213 / loads 0.213 / 32 MB at 63.5k events (3.4 us per event folded)
data.question: Does a persisted folded-State checkpoint beat folding the log on this 63.5k-event log, after the claim-window and renewal fast paths?

data.body: B-gap-log-scale step 4 (a verified folded-State checkpoint) was NOT built: R-logscale-checkpoint-2026-10-15 measured pickle.loads of the State at 0.213 s against 0.213 s to fold the same 63.5k events (32 MB pickle), so a checkpoint of the whole State saves nothing at this size. What remains linear and dominates now: the read snapshot's marshal load of every parsed event (~0.5 s at 63.5k events, scales with N), the fold (3.4 us/event), and the per-command second folds listed in B-logscale-fold-once. Revisit when the fold passes ~2 s (about 600k events) or with a representation that loads in O(tail): per-item state keyed to the shard prefix hash, loaded lazily. Rules for any attempt: valid only for the exact sorted-event prefix it covers (hash of the ids in (lamport, agent, id) order; a shard merge that inserts earlier events must fall back to a full fold), extend the ONE existing read snapshot file (no second mechanism), `fold` must resume with its adopted-orphan pre-scan, byte-identical repr(items) against a full fold on this log and a generated 10x log.
data.title: Log scale: make loading the folded state cheaper than folding it (the fold checkpoint, if it can pay)

data.body: B-gap-log-scale made status and next fold once and passed the State into scan. Still folding more than once (counted by tests/test_fold_once.py, which pins status and next at 1 and brief at <=2): brief folds 2-3 times (_load, store.ensure which returns an unlocalized State, scan); heartbeat 2 (_load, the decide fold in _transition); `hooks session-start` 6 (upgrade_plan repair_items and migration_items each fold via repairs.context, enforce.drift_base, cadence/external-sync loads). Pass one State down (a per-command State is safe to share only if callers do not mutate it: localize mutates, so copy or make it pure first). Add each command to the fold-count test with its measured number.
data.title: Log scale: one fold per command for brief, heartbeat and the session hooks

data.body: B-gap-log-scale moved large gate evidence into .ddflow/blobs/<aa>/<sha256>.json (committed with the shards by services.eventcommit). Anything that copies, archives or restores the event log must carry the blobs too, or the restored log shows evidence as unavailable (doctor reports it as a problem): B-gap-log-backup, `ddflow export`, `ddflow import`, upgrade backups (services.backups) and any `git add .ddflow/events` instruction in docs. Add a restore test: back up, delete the project's .ddflow, restore, `ddflow doctor` is clean and LB.full resolves every stub. Also a gc: blobs no event references (after a log truncation) can be listed by `ddflow doctor` as a note and removed by an explicit command; never automatically.
data.title: Log scale: backup, export and import carry .ddflow/blobs
